course_title: Anatomy & Neuroanatomy Fundamentals for Speech Pathologists

learning_outcomes.description: Describe the main anatomy and neuroanatomy of the head, neck and thorax involved in human communication and swallowing.
Identify the brain areas and cranial nerves involved in human communication and swallowing.
Explain the relationship between structure and function of sensory and effector systems involved in communication and swallowing, including their main deficits in humans.
Recognise the clinical presentation of individuals with communication and swallowing disorders, including techniques can be utilised for diagnosis and intervention.
Apply knowledge of anatomy and neuroanatomy to the describe the clinical presentation of individuals with communication and swallowing disorders.
Recognise and adhere to ethical principles when participating in human cadaveric learning.

assessments.task_description:
In-class spotter quizzes will cover content (practical and lectures) from previous weeks. The Quizzes will be held during scheduled practical class time.

  • Each quiz consists of 20 multiple-choice questions using anatomical models and specimens.
  • Students will have approximately 1 minute to complete each question.
  • A total of three (3) quizzes will be conducted across the semester.
  • ALL quiz scores will count towards the final grade.
  • Each quiz contributes 10%, for a total of 30% of the final course grade.
  • These quizzes are closed-book and should be completed independently, without access to notes or electronic devices.
  • Students will have access to the quiz questions, pinned specimens and correct answers for review immediately after the quiz during scheduled class
  • Students should bring their Student ID, usual PPE and also bring pencils, pens and erasers to complete this assessment.

Additional information is available on the Blackboard site and will be covered during the course introduction.

This assessment task is to be completed in-person. The use of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) or Machine Translation (MT) tools will not be permitted. Any attempted use of AI or MT may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct.
assessments.submission_guidelines: We recommend that students use a 2B or HB pencil to complete the answer sheet and write their name in upper case to assist the electronic marking of the questions.

There will be approximately 1 minute per question and students will move around the GAF to different stations.

Clipboards will be provided.
